title: Logspace preimages
statement: Let $f$ map finite binary strings to finite binary strings, and suppose its output length is bounded by $C(|x|+1)^c$ for some natural numbers $C,c$. Suppose also that each of the following languages is in $\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$: the language of pairs $(x,i)$ for which the $i$th bit of $f(x)$ is $1$, and the language of pairs $(x,i)$ for which $i<|f(x)|$, with pairs represented by the encoding that doubles the bits of the first string, appends the separator $01$, and then the second string. Then for every language $A\in\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$, the language $\{x:f(x)\in A\}$ is in $\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ has output length at most $C(|x|+1)^c$ for some $C,c\in\mathbb N$
The language of pairs $(x,i)$ whose $i$th output bit under $f$ is $1$ belongs to $\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$
The language of pairs $(x,i)$ with $i<|f(x)|$ belongs to $\mathsf{LOGSPACE}$
